$comment: Model aliases by intelligence tier, plus the permission reviewer's chain. Aliases cannot target other aliases, so every entry is a concrete model. A tier carries one opencode-go rung, not a stack: the Go quota is shared, so a drained pool fails every Go model at once and a second rung only helps if the first model's own monthly cap binds, which for a cheap model's 250M+ tokens it never does (ADR-0125). Rung order inside a tier is ADR-0103's — lead by capability, then turn completion observed here, then agentic benchmark evidence, then price — and prices, caps and scores are deliberately absent because they move between syncs (ADR-0118): read them from `bin/pi-model-cost`. Rejected alternatives live in `$bench` below: one entry per model this file mentions or `enabledModels` enables but no chain places, with why it is out and what would promote it. `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` scores above every rung here at a lower drain, but its endpoint trains on request data and it is on trial outside the tiers until that trade is judged — select it directly. A tier spans claude-bridge, opencode-go, openai-codex and the free opencode-go models because those are the separate pools, which is the only availability hedge a rung list can hold — but claude-bridge splits one five-hour window across every tier, so it commits in proportion to how much traffic the earlier tiers already sent (ADR-0125 has the measurements). `glm-5.3` is the Go rung behind `top` and `mid`: `deepseek-v4.1-flash` wins four of the eight weighted evaluations but loses Terminal-Bench 4.0 and CritPt v2 by eight points each, which are the two closest to this agent's work. `cheap` keeps `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, whose turns ask for less, at a tenth of the token price and a lower drain outside peak hours; `top` therefore leads with Opus opportunistically and expects to run glm-5.3, then codex's gpt-5.6-terra when Go's window is spent too; the free models close `cheap` and `mid` after every scored rung (ADR-0120) with one reviewer prompt each as their only evidence, and beam-free takes no images so it stays reviewer-only. `reviewer` is ordered for latency and availability rather than capability: Gemini's free tier and the free Go models answer in 1-2s once the paid quotas are gone, while Haiku averages ~10s of session startup, so firstEventMs stays 30s to cover Haiku's tail and gemini-3.5-flash-lite's 28s. claude-bridge serves the reviewer only through the pi-claude-bridge#216 standalone-prompt patches and refuses a follow-up review's multi-turn conversation either way, hence followUpReviews off. Groq stays out: its free tiers cap at 2-8k TPM against a ~14k-token reviewer prompt.

opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor.out: its endpoint trains on request data, so every prompt through it is training data
opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor.promote: the trial in docs/BACKLOG.md says the consent is worth it; it then displaces deepseek-v4.1-flash in cheap

opencode-go/hy4.out: scores above glm-5.3 but burns several times as fast and carries a smaller cap, so it can neither lead nor sit behind it
opencode-go/hy4.promote: top needs another rung from the same pool and that burn is accepted

opencode-go/gemini-4-argon.out: the cheapest route to top-class capability, blocked by a cap that a handful of hard turns spends
opencode-go/gemini-4-argon.promote: top turns need what glm-5.3 cannot give and the pool cost is accepted

opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro.out: below glm-5.3 on both the agentic evaluations and the composite, on a smaller cap
opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro.promote: its terms improve or the tier it would serve drops below it

opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code.out: no composite, and it fails Terminal-Bench 4.0 outright while promising on other evals
opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code.promote: AA scores it, and its Terminal-Bench 4.0 result proves to be a harness artefact rather than a capability signal

opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-pro.out: a documented tool-call repetition failure mode keeps it below every rung with a clean record
opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-pro.promote: the failure mode is fixed in a later revision

opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash.out: the same family as glm-5.3 with less capability and no larger cap, so it never outlives it
opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash.promote: glm-5.3's cap or price changes enough to separate them

opencode-go/minimax-m3.1-flash.out: cheaper per token than the rungs above it but with the smallest cap in the pool, so it locks out first
opencode-go/minimax-m3.1-flash.promote: the pool's leaders cap out and this one's cap rises

claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-2.out: the highest score the harness can reach, blocked by sharing one five-hour window with every tier, which mid needs first
claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-2.promote: a window of its own appears, or mid stops leading with sonnet-5-5
